items.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: The people when they really got to enjoying Glenn Miller and Benny Goodman, jitterbugged.

ctx.x: Marvelous. What effect did the dancing that was so connected with jazz, and at the end of World War II I guess, do you have a take on what kind of happened at that point?

Well a number of things happened. Number one America got out of the dance phase quote unquote. The art of dance was very, very important both to jazz and vice versa. Not only in Hollywood, but in the early days of jazz, jazz was associated with dancing. Even Glenn Miller quote unquote jazz. The people when they really got to enjoying Glenn Miller and Benny Goodman, jitterbugged. So it wasn’t just music to crowd around the bandstand and listen to, it was music to dance to and the same thing was true with Ellington…

I sometimes wonder if there wasn’t enough stress after World War II. I mean the dancing could have been a release because there were tough times and there was a war and all that, and when that went away, maybe people didn’t feel that need to—
